title: Average Plumber Salary Australia: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and What You Really Take Home
description: Discover the average plumber salary Australia based on award rates and ABS data. Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual, including casual loading, super, and tax.
salarySummary: Based on the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020, a qualified plumber (Level 1 tradesperson) earns a minimum of $29.45 per hour, or about $1,119.10 per week for a 38-hour week, equating to an annual salary of approximately $58,193 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the average plumber salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The average plumber salary in Australia varies by source. The Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020 sets a minimum hourly rate of $29.45 for a Level 1 tradesperson, equating to about $58,193 per year for a 38-hour week. However, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports median full-time earnings of $1,990 per week (about $47 per hour), which is higher due to experience, overtime, and allowances. The award rate is the legal minimum, while the median reflects what many plumbers actually earn.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a plumber's pay?
faqs.a: Under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020, casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1 tradesperson, that means $36.81 per hour instead of $29.45. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals don't receive. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) calculator, you enter the base hourly rate and check the casual box – never include the loading in the rate you type.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the award rate and the median earnings for plumbers?
faqs.a: The award rate is the legal minimum set by the Fair Work Commission for each classification under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020. For a Level 1 tradesperson, that's $29.45 per hour. Median earnings, from the ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2025), are $47 per hour for full-time plumbers. The gap reflects factors like experience, overtime, penalty rates, and allowances that push actual pay above the minimum. The award ensures a floor, but many plumbers earn significantly more.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Average Plumber Salary Australia

If you're researching the **average plumber salary Australia**, you'll find a range of figures depending on whether you look at award minimums or real-world earnings. Plumbers install, maintain and repair pipes, drains, guttering, mechanical services and related equipment – a skilled trade that commands solid pay. This article breaks down how hourly rates translate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly amounts, and explains the role of casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### Award Minimum Rates for Plumbers

The legal minimum pay for plumbers comes from the **Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020**. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) that summarise these rates. For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week, the minimum weekly rate for a **Plumbing and mechanical services tradesperson/Sprinkler fitter tradesperson Level 1** is $1,119.10, which equals $29.45 per hour. Higher classifications – such as special class or advanced tradesperson – pay more, up to $33.77 per hour for an Advanced Level 2.

To calculate annual pay from an award hourly rate, use the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a Level 1 tradesperson: $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193.20 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The fortnightly pay would be $1,119.10 × 2 = $2,238.20.

### Median Earnings from ABS Data

While the award sets the floor, the **Australian Bureau of Statistics** (ABS) provides a picture of what plumbers actually earn. According to Jobs and Skills Australia, the median full-time earnings for plumbers are $1,990 per week, or about $47 per hour. That's based on the ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours, May 2025. This median is higher than the award rate because it includes experienced workers, overtime, and allowances. The average full-time hours worked are 44 per week, but the median earnings figure already reflects those hours.

For comparison, the on-site reference shows ABS Average Weekly Earnings for all full-time adult ordinary time employees at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). Plumbers' median of $1,990 is close to that national average.

### How to Calculate Your Annual Pay

Whether you're on an award rate or a negotiated salary, the conversion is straightforward. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or do it manually:

- **Weekly**: hourly rate × hours per week (assume 38 if full-time under the award)
- **Fortnightly**: weekly × 2
- **Annual**: weekly × 52 (or hourly × 38 × 52)

If you work more than 38 hours, your ordinary time pay is still based on 38 hours; overtime is paid at higher rates (typically 1.5x or 2x) and is not included in this simple calculation.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual employees under the Plumbing Award receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1 tradesperson, that's $29.45 + 25% = $36.81 per hour. This loading replaces entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) calculator, enter the base rate (e.g., $29.45) and check the casual box – do not type $36.81.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a plumber earning the award rate of $58,193, super adds about $6,983 per year. For the median earner at $103,480 ($1,990 × 52), super would be about $12,418, but note the cap applies if earnings exceed $270,830.

### Tax Considerations

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a plumber earning $58,193 (award minimum), tax would be approximately $8,667 plus Medicare $1,164, leaving about $48,362 take-home. For the median earner at $103,480, tax would be around $24,467 plus Medicare $2,070, leaving about $76,943. These are estimates; your actual tax depends on deductions, HELP repayments, and other factors.

### Putting It All Together

The **average plumber salary Australia** spans from the award minimum of about $58,000 per year to a median of around $103,000. Your actual pay depends on your classification, experience, location, and whether you work overtime or receive allowances. For a personalised estimate, use our [reference tables](/data) to find your award rate, then apply the formulas above.

Remember: annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
